I farm the way I know best: I keep the wheat-maize rotation on most of my land because it is steady, familiar, and works well with my well irrigation. I am 69 years old, so I will not make the year too complicated or too labor-intensive. I will put 8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 8 mu, because that rotation gives me grain for income and uses the land efficiently. I will keep 4 mu in cotton, because I already know how to grow it and it spreads my risk. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stand establishment, but I will not push inputs too high because fertilizer and labor both cost money. With irrigation from the well, I will water at the key times rather than too often. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for my household to manage than deep ploughing, and I will keep pesticide sprays to the level needed to protect the crop rather than spraying too much.
